question_text: A local government unit in Mindanao passes an ordinance that restricts the right to freedom of assembly for certain groups, citing public safety. A resident challenges the ordinance, arguing it violates the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR). Under Philippine law, which statement best describes the legal effect of the UDHR in this situation?

options.text: The UDHR is directly enforceable as law in the Philippines, so the ordinance is automatically void.
The UDHR is not a treaty and has no binding effect, but it may be used as a guide for interpreting Philippine laws and policies.
The UDHR is a treaty ratified by the Philippines, so it has the force of law and overrides the ordinance.
The UDHR is a customary international law that automatically prevails over any local ordinance.
